# Combo Box

Select one or multiple options in a large list, either by typing a value directly or by choosing inside the list.
See <a className="sbk-link" href="https://design-system.airbus.corp/components/combo-box/design/" target="_blank">ComboBox guidelines<i className="ds-icon-launch"></i></a>

### When to use

To select a single value in a small list, consider using the <LinkTo kind="Components/Select" story="docs">Select</LinkTo> component instead.

<Source code="import { ComboBox } from &#x22;@airbus/components-react&#x22;" />

<Primary />

<Controls />

- Any other props supplied will be provided to the `Input` HTML element

### No match

Open the list of options to see content displayed when no items match input value.<br />
Customize this content with the `renderNoMatch` prop.

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.NoMatch} />

### Multiple selection

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.Multiple} />

### Limit size

Use `limitChips` prop if you want the ComboBox to limit the size of the component with multiple selection.

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.LimitSize} />

### Grouped Options

Use `groupBy` method to define group names based on options data.<br />
This feature is **incompatible with virtualization**.

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.GroupedOptions} />

### Dark Mode

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.Dark} />

Details about implementing dark mode is available in <LinkTo kind="General/Visual Styles/Introduction" story="docs">Visual styles Page</LinkTo>

### Controlled

Options can be of types `string` or `object`. The `value` prop has to be specified in the same types.
In `single` mode, the `value` prop can be a `string` or an `object`.<br />
In `multiple` mode, the `value` prop can be an array of `string` or an array `object`.

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.Controlled} />

### Default input value

Using `defaultInputValue` prop, you can set a default text to prefilter the list of options.

In multiple mode, you can also use the `keepInputOnSelect` boolean to avoid reset of input value when selecting an option.
It allows to select multiple options with the same filter.

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.DefaultInput} />

### Custom options and labels

If you provide custom option types, use the `getOptionLabel` and `getOptionValue` to define how to get a value and a label.

The default option format is `{ label: string, value: string, disabled: boolean }`.

You can also use the `getChipLabel` method to customize the label of the selected options in multiple mode.

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.CustomOptions} />

### Locked options

To lock some options, use the `hideClearOnDisabled` prop and a custom onChange handler that will force fixed options.

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.LockedOptions} />

### Filter match

Several matching algorithm are available to filter the list of options when typing text.<br />
By default all options which label contains the string will be displayed.<br />
See [match-sorter documentation](https://github.com/kentcdodds/match-sorter).

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.FilterMatch} />

### Creatable

Using `creatable` and `onCreate` props, it allows users to add new options to the list dynamically.

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.Creatable} />

Example without any predefined options

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.CreatableEmpty} />

The `onCreate` callback allow to define the format of the new option.
It can also be used for asynchronous scenario, if for example your want to let the user define the new option in a Dialog.

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.CreatableDialog} />

### Virtualized

With a very large amount of options, use `allowVirtualization` to optimize performance.
The example below provides 10 000 options.

You can use `keepInputOnSelect` to allow selection of multiple options with the same prefix.

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.Virtualized} />

### Copy Paste

Additional props are passed through to the underlying html input.<br />
In this example we implement `onPaste` input event handler to allow copy pasting multiple values separated by spaces or commas.<br />
Examples : `Rust, Elixir` or `Kotlin JavaScript`

<Canvas of={ComboBoxStories.CopyPaste} />
